claim_summary: For the five-regular Clebsch graph on sixteen vertices, the minimum power-dominating sets are exactly the 160 independent triples and 160 induced three-vertex paths. The complement of the initial closed neighborhood of each optimum \(S\) is another optimum \(U(S)\) of the opposite type, and \(U\) is a fixed-point-free involution. The 320 optimal placements have a connected 21-regular token-jump graph with 3,360 edges and diameter three, and a connected token-slide graph with 1,120 edges and diameter six. Every \(S\) has exactly one slide-distance-six state, namely \(U(S)\), at jump distance three; the maximum slide-versus-jump distance excess is three, achieved exactly by the 160 pairs \(\{S,U(S)\}\). All assertions are for the sixteen-vertex five-regular graph, not its ten-regular complement.
integrity: Two independently implemented exhaustive standard-library checkers reproduced all 696 low-cardinality seed decisions, 320 minimum states, legal move graphs and complete pairwise shortest distances. Evidence is same-project computational checking, not external independent scientific validation.
scientific_limitations: Finite theorem restricted to the five-regular, sixteen-vertex Clebsch graph and minimum power-dominating placements. Does not imply a family theorem or measured physical sensor deployment performance; possible unindexed historical priority remains.
title: Blind-spot antipodes and the sharp relocation gap of the five-regular Clebsch graph
